Compiling an inventory

Source: vignettes/compiling-inventory.Rmd
compiling-inventory.Rmd

stand_table() expands tree counts, basal area, log counts, and product quantities. stock_table() uses the same calculation with product and diameter-class grouping by default. Both require the complete inventory and supplied expansion factors.

## Use the complete simulated heights and retain tree identifiers
trees <- example_trees_pnw %>%
  mutate(id = tree, ht = ht_simulated)
## Load the inventory specifications
specifications <- example_products(name = 'pnw')
## Apply the product table to the inventory
result <- merchandise(dbh = trees$dbh,
                      ht = trees$ht,
                      species = trees$species,
                      id = trees$id,
                      products = specifications,
                      status = TRUE)

Stand and stock tables 

## Expand tree counts and quantities by species
stand <- stand_table(x = result,
                     trees = trees,
                     expansion = trees$expansion_factor,
                     by = 'species')
species merchandising_status trees_per_acre failed_trees_per_acre basal_area_ft2_per_acre logs_per_acre net_scale_board_foot_per_acre net_scale_green_short_ton_per_acre
Douglas-fir valid 226.4 0 375.053 623.6 76492 18.523
western hemlock valid 73.6 0 119.577 194.4 21908 5.944 
## Expand stock by product
stock <- stock_table(x = result,
                     trees = trees,
                     expansion = trees$expansion_factor,
                     by = 'product')
product merchandising_status trees_per_acre failed_trees_per_acre basal_area_ft2_per_acre logs_per_acre net_scale_board_foot_per_acre net_scale_green_short_ton_per_acre
export valid 149.2 0 390.155 228.8 77900 0.000
domestic_saw valid 243.2 0 475.100 282.4 20500 0.000
pulp valid 300.0 0 494.630 306.8 0 24.467

trees$id joins the inventory to the result. Expansion follows the caller’s inventory row order. area_unit labels expansion without converting it. These are weighted sums without variance estimates.

A tree contributing to multiple products appears in each product group. Omit product from grouping to count each tree once in its inventory group. Different measurement units receive separate quantity columns.

Product summaries

product_summary() summarizes a saved result. table = 'logs' groups by product and measurement fields. table = 'trees' summarizes tree quantities. na_action = 'propagate' retains missing quantities in totals.

## Sum log quantities by product
summary <- product_summary(x = result,
                           table = 'logs',
                           expansion = trees$expansion_factor,
                           na_action = 'propagate')
product scale_unit input_trees net_scale
domestic_saw board_foot 243 20500.000
export board_foot 148 77900.000
pulp green_short_ton 300 24.467 
## Calculate product totals directly from inventory measurements
direct <- product_summary_by_tree(dbh = trees$dbh,
                                  ht = trees$ht,
                                  species = trees$species,
                                  products = specifications,
                                  status = TRUE)
product scale_unit input_trees net_scale
domestic_saw board_foot 243 20670.000
export board_foot 148 78140.000
pulp green_short_ton 300 24.587

The direct call uses unexpanded totals unless expansion is supplied. merch_summary() is the deprecated name for product_summary() and returns the same table.

## Summarize a saved result through the compatibility name
legacy <- merch_summary(x = result, table = 'trees')
input_trees log_count log_net_cubic_ib
300 818 21522.41 
## Add selected log counts to the complete example tree list
counts <- example_trees %>%
  transmute(tree,
            logs = tree_log_count(dbh = dbh,
                                  ht = ht,
                                  species = species,
                                  model = model,
                                  products = specifications))
tree logs
1 2
2 2
3 2
4 3
5 3
6 4

Stand and stock tables retain valid zero-log trees, failures, and trees absent from the result. merchandising_status separates those groups. Missing quantities propagate within applicable groups.
